headline: AI-spending jitters and a looming Fed meeting unsettle risk appetite
body: Overnight trade carried a cautious tone into Friday: Asian markets followed Wall Street's AI-and-chip-led softness, with Japan's Nikkei down roughly 1.4% and S&P 500 futures hovering near 7,650, little changed to slightly lower. Semiconductor and AI-infrastructure names remain the epicenter, echoing selloffs that have recurred through the summer and fall as investors periodically reassess hyperscaler capex payoff timelines. Commodity moves complicate a simple risk-off read: crude has pushed higher on supply-side jitters even as gold slipped to a three-month low and silver gave back a large chunk of its recent surge, a combination that looks more like a profit-taking unwind in crowded trades than a classic flight to safety. The options market shows a put/call ratio near the mid-0.9s, on the richer side of recent ranges, consistent with traders adding modest hedges rather than chasing the rally unchecked.

Behind the daily noise, two slower-moving concerns are doing more to shape positioning: the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, where rate-path uncertainty persists after a stretch of elevated long-end yields, and the approaching midterm elections, which commentary increasingly flags as a source of headline risk even though historical studies find the link to long-run returns thin. Both are the kind of event-risk that tends to get priced defensively in the run-up rather than resolved cleanly beforehand. Retail and social chatter offered no distinct signal today - no clear meme-stock spike or crowd-positioning extreme turned up in a scan of the usual forums - so this read leans more on index-level price action and macro headlines than on crowd sentiment data, a sign that retail enthusiasm has cooled rather than spiked in either direction.
